correctness.rationale: The proof's load-bearing mechanism is sound. The regular-polygon gauge is linear on each cone generated by adjacent vertices. In each of the two residue classes \(N\equiv4,8\pmod{12}\), the explicit moving triangle is piecewise affine; the derivative of each side vector is parallel to the corresponding unit-sphere edge, while endpoint determinant inequalities keep the whole affine side path inside one cone. Hence each side norm is constant on a piece, and endpoint reflections identify the three constants. The two pieces meet continuously, dihedral symmetry covers the boundary, and the cited uniqueness-through-a-boundary-point proposition converts the construction into constancy for all triangles in \(\mathcal T_3\). A fresh direct gauge reconstruction reproduced the claimed constant side lengths for representative values including \(N=16\) and \(N=32\).
